description.p: Reverie is a media player for Linux with Milkdrop-style visualisations built in — not running alongside in a second window, but rendered into the same scene as the rest of the interface.

It exists because the available options sit at two extremes: players that look like they were designed in 2009, and library-management applications that happen to play audio. Reverie is neither. It plays what you give it, shows something worth looking at while it does, and does not try to organise your music collection.

ul.li: Milkdrop visualisations driven by the decoded audio, embedded or fullscreen
Adaptive visual quality that holds a frame-rate target, so it stays usable without a GPU
One playlist: drag to reorder, multi-select, save and load M3U
Video on the same surface, with subtitles and audio track selection
A ten-band equaliser with twelve preset curves
Ten colour palettes plus a custom theme editor; follows the desktop light/dark setting
A compact mini-player, and media key support through MPRIS

description.p: Deliberately not included: library management, lyrics, social features and third-party service integration.

Please note: the visualisations flash and change quickly, as Milkdrop presets are built to. If you are sensitive to flashing lights they can be turned off entirely, and everything else works exactly the same. Reverie asks once, on first run, before anything has played.

description.p: Following the desktop's light/dark setting now works inside a Flatpak, where the sandbox cannot read the desktop's settings directly.
Alternate video streams no longer stall playback, and can be chosen when a file has them. Packaging for Flathub, and new screenshots.
Window title fixes, and a maximised window now stays maximised after fullscreen.
Subtitles, audio and subtitle track selection with preferred languages, and hardware decoding where the machine supports it.
